content.value_statement: Designers and app teams need fast guidance for Apple content components. This skill maps common content needs to HIG-backed component choices and accessibility requirements.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Apple content components for charts, collections, images, web content, sharing, color selection, and lockups.
Summarizes HIG guidance for component selection, configuration, accessibility, and platform behavior.
Provides platform notes for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS when the references include them.
Helps compare standard components such as Swift Charts, UICollectionView, WKWebView, image views, and activity views.
Prompts for missing context before recommending a component when content type, platform, or scale is unclear.
limitations: It is a reference skill, not a replacement for Apple documentation or platform testing.
It does not generate production-ready Swift, SwiftUI, UIKit, AppKit, or WebKit implementations by itself.
It covers content display components, not the full Apple Human Interface Guidelines.
It may not include Apple guidance published after the bundled reference files were created.

use_cases.title: Choose the Right Content Component
use_cases.description: Map a product requirement to a chart, collection, image view, web view, activity view, color well, image well, or lockup.

use_cases.title: Review Apple Platform Fit
use_cases.description: Check whether a planned content component matches iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, or visionOS conventions.

use_cases.title: Improve Content Accessibility
use_cases.description: Identify accessibility needs for charts, images, collections, and other content display patterns before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to show [content type] in an Apple app for [platform]. Recommend the best HIG content component and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [component A] and [component B] for [use case] on [platform]. Include accessibility, interaction, and platform notes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this screen concept for Apple HIG content component fit: [screen description]. Identify mismatches, accessibility gaps, and better component choices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Component Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a HIG-aligned specification for [content component] in [app context]. Include rationale, configuration guidance, accessibility requirements, and platform-specific notes.

output_examples.input: We need to show weekly fitness data on iPhone and Apple Watch.
output_examples.output: Recommended component: Swift Charts. Use simple marks for watchOS, avoid complex chart interactions, and provide clear summaries and VoiceOver support.

output_examples.input: A macOS app needs users to select and replace a profile image.
output_examples.output: Recommended component: image well. It supports drag and drop, copy, paste, and deletion, which matches editable image selection on macOS.

output_examples.input: An app wants to show short web help pages inside a settings flow.
output_examples.output: Recommended component: WKWebView for brief embedded content. Provide navigation only when needed and avoid using it to recreate a full browser.

best_practices: Start with the standard Apple component before designing a custom content interaction.
Include accessibility labels, summaries, and navigation behavior when content conveys important information.
Check platform support before applying a component across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, or visionOS.
anti_patterns: Using a custom layout when a standard row, grid, chart, image view, or share sheet already fits the need.
Relying only on color, visual position, or gestures to communicate essential content information.
Treating this bundled reference as a substitute for current Apple documentation and hands-on testing.

faq.question: What components does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers charts, collections, image views, image wells, color wells, web views, activity views, and lockups.

faq.question: Can it write production Apple app code?
faq.answer: It can guide component choice and configuration, but it does not provide complete production implementations by itself.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights accessibility needs such as labels, VoiceOver behavior, Audio Graphs, and clear content summaries.

faq.question: Which platforms are considered?
faq.answer: The references include guidance for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS, and visionOS when applicable.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when deciding how to display content in an Apple app or reviewing content components against HIG guidance.

faq.question: Does it replace the official Apple HIG?
faq.answer: No. It is a bundled reference helper and should be checked against current Apple documentation for final decisions.
